title: Zero critical Hausdorff measure of a nonconstant-offspring Galton–Watson tree boundary
source_version: Probability on Trees and Networks, author paperback version 2026-08-19

difficulty_reason: The selected author proof establishes the critical no-flow obstruction for unbounded finite-mean offspring via the independent subtree recursion, a truncated expectation and an essential-supremum argument, then reads it in the critical Hausdorff covering gauge. This is the critical proof itself, not a theorem citation only.
selected_claim: Exercise 15.26, in the intrinsic tree-boundary metric. For any Galton–Watson offspring random variable L with finite mean m>1, the log m-dimensional Hausdorff measure of the boundary is almost surely zero when L is nonconstant. The deterministic offspring exception is preserved.

§15.1, definition of Hausdorff measure and equivalence of zero unconstrained covering content to zero Hausdorff measure for positive exponent.

source_caveats: Select the first part of Theorem 5.35 only, through the essential-supremum step at critical mean. The separate supercritical positive-flow direction is outside the selection.

For A_i=1/m and nonconstant L the printed exceptional local sum condition fails, since the sum is L/m. Finite mean suffices. The selected author proof assumes neither a bounded offspring count nor an L log L moment nor conditioning on survival.

For a general tree the diameter of a cylinder is at most exp(−|x|). Equality is printed in the case of two children with infinite descendants, so the critical zero-measure bridge uses only the upper bound and the cutset-cover correspondence.

Hawkes and Falconer 1987 full texts were not obtained at the checked publisher and archive endpoints. Graf Theorems 7.6–7.7 were read from the publisher PDF in a fixed-N separated Euclidean similarity model. Historical references are separate from the proof spans.
The original sentence ends with the constant-offspring exception. It asks for zero measure for nonconstant L and makes no separate numerical or positive claim for constant L.
